content: ALG2, also known as Alpha-1,3-mannosyltransferase ALG2, is an enzyme that is encoded by the ALG2 gene in humans. Mutations in the ALG2 gene are linked to congenital defects in glycosylation processes. This gene encodes a protein that belongs to the glycosyltransferase 1 family. The protein functions as an alpha-1,3-mannosyltransferase, which is responsible for transferring mannose residues to specific dolichol-linked oligosaccharides. Specifically, it catalyzes the mannosylation of Man(2)GlcNAc(2)-dolichol diphosphate and Man(1)GlcNAc(2)-dolichol diphosphate to produce Man(3)GlcNAc(2)-dolichol diphosphate. Defects in the ALG2 gene have been associated with a condition known as congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ih (CDG-Ii), a rare metabolic disorder that affects glycoprotein biosynthesis. Additionally, ALG2 has been demonstrated to interact with other proteins, including ANXA7 (Annexin A7) and ANXA11 (Annexin A11), suggesting its involvement in broader cellular processes.
